inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares, Q2 2026 10-Q (119.751m). Held FLAT: SBC (plus equity-award withholding tax) is expensed in the flows, so buybacks are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and are value-neutral here. No non-SBC issuance.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement via SEC XBRL: ShareBasedCompensation $80.070M + PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $76.917M (no combined adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation figure published, so the two lines are summed). FY2025 withholding is elevated by large performance-award vestings at a higher share price; FY2019-24 it ran $15-32M.
inputs.buyback_note: Genuine repurchaser: $354.7M FY2025, $432.2M in H1 2026 (financing-activity outflow, not authorisation). The flat count is funded, not a modelling convention.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: OCF $914.519M less purchases of property & equipment $19.628M less purchases and development of software $50.915M (FY2025). The Metrics.csv FreeCashFlow ($894.9M) omits capitalised software; the true reported FCF is $844.0M.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.95 -> cost of equity ~9.1%; debt ~$1.7bn against ~$17.6bn market cap (~9% of capital) at ~5.5% pre-tax / ~4.3% after tax -> WACC ~8.5%. Same WACC in every scenario: freight-cycle risk is charged in the scenario paths and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (office space, ~$288M liability at 2026-06-30): lease cost sits inside operating expense and therefore inside EBITDA; lease liabilities are NOT in net debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the cyclical adaptations. CHRW is an asset-light freight broker/forwarder -- an operating company whose value is a free-cash-flow stream, so it routes to owner-FCF (no prior valuation or memory entry to be consistent with). CYCLICAL / MID-CYCLE FRAMING: gross revenue swings with freight rates (FY2022 $24.7bn -> FY2023 $17.6bn) and is a poor base; the FY2025 revenue decline (-8.4%) mixes the Europe Surface Transportation divestiture, lower ocean pricing and fuel surcharges. The build therefore compounds from FY2025 revenue but lets margins, not the FY2025 FCF, carry the judgment: year 1 is anchored to FY2026 guidance (operating income $964M-$1.04bn, reaffirmed at Q2 2026 with an assumed -3% freight market), which is a trough-volume year delivering management's 'mid-cycle' margin through Lean-AI cost-out (headcount -31% since 2022). The base then assumes a partial cycle recovery to a ~7.0-7.2% pre-SBC EBITDA margin on gross revenue, above the pre-2023 range (5.8-6.6% pre-SBC) to credit the structural cost-out, and does not extrapolate the FY2021-22 peak. FY2025 owner FCF ($687M) was flattered by working-capital release as revenue fell; H1 2026 OCF of only $104M shows the reverse as revenue grew 9%, so wc_capture is NEGATIVE (-8% of the revenue change: receivables exceed carrier payables). EBITDA margin paths are PRE-SBC (GAAP OI + D&A + SBC); FY2025 was 6.02% of revenue. Capex paths include capitalised software (FY2026 guide $65-75M). Cash tax: FY2025 cash taxes $95.0M on $722.5M pretax (13.2%); FY2026 ETR guide 18-20%, ramped to 21%.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is not usable: book value is driven by buybacks ($1.46bn in FY2022 alone cut equity 33%), so equity 5yr -0.4% vs EPS 5yr +5.5% and equity 3yr +10.9% vs revenue 3yr -13.1% diverge by far more than 30%. All 3- and 5-year windows are cycle-distorted (FY2022 peak, FY2020 pre-boom), so the full-cycle revenue CAGR is selected instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on an owner-FCF series (CSV FCF less SBC less equity-award withholding tax). Pre-FY2024 capitalised software is not in the CSV capex, so the series is consistent with itself but slightly above true owner FCF. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-20.5%) sits below reported (-17.2%) because withholding tax jumped from $28M (FY2022) to $77M (FY2025) -- more of the reported cash flow is being paid away in equity comp.

base.rationale: FY2026 revenue ~$17.9bn (H1 +9.3%, Q2 +19.3% on truckload rate tightening) with pre-SBC EBITDA ~6.6% = GAAP OI ~$1.0bn guide midpoint + D&A ~$95M + SBC ~$105M. Partial freight recovery lifts margin to ~7.1%, then settles at 7.0% as some Lean-AI savings are competed away. Revenue long-run 3-4.5%, near the 18-year through-cycle 4.5%. Cap 15x (asset-light, high ROIC, but cyclical); Gordon at 8.5%/2.5% would be ~17x.

bull.rationale: Freight cycle turns in 2027 on top of a structurally leaner cost base: operating leverage takes pre-SBC EBITDA to 8% of gross revenue (well above the FY2018 peak of 6.6%), and NAST keeps taking share.

bear.rationale: FY2026 lands at the low end of guidance, then a tariff/recession leg extends the trough into 2027 and digital brokers compress take-rates: margin falls back to the pre-Lean-AI range (~5.2-5.5% pre-SBC) and stays there.

scenario_narratives.base: C.H. Robinson delivers FY2026 guidance (~$1.0bn operating income) in a still-contracting freight market, proving that most of the Lean-AI cost-out (headcount down ~31% since 2022 with volumes up) is structural. The truckload market tightens gradually rather than snapping back; NAST keeps outgrowing the Cass index but Global Forwarding stays tariff-volatile. Pre-SBC EBITDA settles near 7% of gross revenue -- above every pre-2023 year but short of a peak-cycle print -- and gross revenue grows 3-5% through the cycle. Working capital absorbs cash as revenue grows because receivables lead carrier payables.
scenario_narratives.bull: The freight cycle inflects in 2027 (truckload costs already up mid-teens YoY) and CHRW captures it with a cost base ~30% leaner than the last upcycle: AGP expands faster than headcount, operating margin prints well above the 'mid-cycle' target, and scale plus Navisphere/AI pricing widen the gap to sub-scale brokers after Convoy's exit. Tariff complexity lifts customs brokerage demand. Pre-SBC EBITDA reaches 8% of gross revenue and holds.
scenario_narratives.bear: The trough extends: new 2026 US tariffs and a USMCA review disrupt cross-border and auto freight, the Cass index keeps falling, and over-cutting headcount shows up in service quality and carrier churn. Digital freight-matching platforms and shipper-direct relationships erode take-rates, so the Lean-AI savings are passed through to customers rather than retained. Margin reverts to the pre-2023 range and revenue stalls.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): freight brokerage is among the most cyclical sectors, the Cass index is still declining and tariff/USMCA policy risk is live, though the balance sheet (net debt ~1.4x EBITDA) carries no solvency risk. Base 50%: FY2026 guidance was reaffirmed with H1 already delivered. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs both a cycle turn and full retention of the AI savings, two things the company does not control equally.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value an asset-light freight broker on the through-cycle owner free cash flow it earns, not on a trough or peak year. Gross revenue is mostly pass-through carrier cost, so the judgment is carried by the margin on gross revenue, anchored to reaffirmed FY2026 guidance and to how much of the Lean-AI cost-out survives a cycle. SBC and the cash tax withheld on vesting awards are charged as the cost they are; buybacks keep the count flat.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin on gross revenue is the whole valuation: each 0.5pp of pre-SBC EBITDA margin is worth roughly $12-14/share in the base case.
Revenue inflates with freight rates, so a rate spike can lift revenue while compressing margin %; the two paths are not independent.
Working capital: a strong upcycle consumes cash (FY2021 OCF was $95M on $844M net income); the -8% capture may understate that in the bull.
Equity-award withholding tax ($77M FY2025, $75M H1 2026) is elevated; if it normalises to ~$25M the SBC charge is too heavy by ~0.2-0.3pp of revenue.
Terminal value carries most of the value; cap multiple 15x base vs Gordon ~17x.
